new.description: Unlock FP/BF16 instruction issue rate on Nvidia 3000's cards to their professional equivalents
new.readme: Unlock FP/BF16 instruction issue rate on Nvidia 3000's cards to their professional equivalents This Linux kernel module combines the CMP unlocker's V67/PLM technique with the pre-driver timing of the UEFI approach. It runs the unlock, writes the speed selectors (SS0 0x88888888, which selects the full BF16 rate, and the 4-bit SS1 0x8 IMLA4) and performs FLR before the unmodified NVIDIA driver binds the card. It is neither a UEFI application nor a patched NVIDIA driver.

new.description: Run iOS and macOS on non-Apple ARM64 hardware through UEFI.
new.readme: An independent project to run iOS and macOS on non-Apple ARM64 hardware through UEFI. Like OpenCore, UniXNU is a general UEFI environment and driver loading system: it loads the drivers a device needs and boots the OS through a common UEFI layer. UniXNU provides shared build tools, ARM64 support, OS profiles and reusable components for ports across SoCs and devices. SoC repositories supply common platform support, and device repositories supply board configuration and hardware integration.

new.description: Incremental rust builds up to 92x faster than cargo/rustc
new.readme: The same commands as cargo, with blaze in front. Blazingly fast Rust, literally. For macOS on Apple silicon and Linux, with or without Rust installed: blaze downloads the Rust it builds with once (about 100 to 135 MB), or uses rustup's. Rather use crates.io or Nix? The first build runs cargo, then waits a few seconds for blaze to load your project. Then change a function and build again: it's back in milliseconds, and the Finished line says [ra-jit] (blaze's engine).

threats.title: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys compromised
threats.headline: Flawed key generation exposed eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys, letting attackers impersonate any website or service
threats.summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were compromised because the CA generated them incorrectly, so anyone can recover them from the certificates. Six are for TLS and chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs. Two are for code signing and trusted by Microsoft. An attacker with any of the keys could impersonate any website or service, and clients that ship their own CA bundle or do not enforce Certificate Transparency are at greater risk.
